en: The *Vajraprabhā-vāta-varṣa-śamana-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of South India during the Great Tang Dynasty.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Bhagavat was surrounded before and behind by a great assembly.
While traveling through the kingdom of Magadha,
he encountered a massive black cloud along the road;
it was dense and heavy, accompanied by a violent, whistling wind.
Amidst thunder, lightning, and the sudden downpour of hail and rain,
he spoke to the Venerable Ānanda:
"You should take a new, clean jar."
With the mantra for filling [the vessel] with water,
one subdues and drives away such as the Naga King Vasuki and all other venomous nagas who afflict the world.
Those who destroy the various crops, flowers, fruits, and seeds, creating calamities,
should all be captured and driven into a jar;
thus shall these winds, clouds, rain, hail, and thunderbolts be stilled.
Then, restrain it.
You shall receive such mantra-dharmas and other methods;
perform the treatment according to the ritual rules.

He addressed the Venerable Ānanda, saying:
"You should first prepare two square maṇḍalas, each measuring two cubits,
by cleanly smearing them with plaster, one before the Buddha and the other on the open road."
First, place a water jar upon the altar before the Buddha.
Holding a willow branch,
insert it into the water jar.
Recite this mantra with a vigorous and rapid voice while stirring the water in a circular motion; thereby,
you shall summon the Naga King Vasuki and all other venomous nagas.
Place them all inside the water jar.
Twenty-one times, one should place the jar upon the ground within the altar so that its mouth reaches the surface of the earth;
this will cause [the time] to become non-seasonal.
Calamities, torrential rains, thunder, hail, and lightning shall all cease at once.
Furthermore, Ānanda, there is a mantra that pacifies all calamities,
obstacles, hot winds, cold winds, whirlwinds, and malignant winds.
It is able to protect all crops, flowers, fruits, and their flavors.

Second, Venerable Ānanda, if one wishes to cultivate these mantra-samayas, one should first,
before the images of the Buddhas of the ten directions,
use various fragrant waters.
Construct a circular maṇḍala, two cubits in size, by applying plaster and decorations.
Furthermore, in a clean open space, construct another pure maṇḍala,
two cubits in size, by applying plaster.
Take one clean, purified one-dou measure jar,
fill it with pure water, and place it upon the altar before the Buddha;
you should offer seasonal incense and flowers as worship.
One should offer incense by burning aloeswood, white sandalwood, frankincense, and so forth; then,
taking a willow branch in hand, one should place it within the water jar.
Recite the mantra with a loud voice and rapid cadence;
this will draw in all venomous dragons, evil winds, torrential rains, calamities, and poisonous vapors,
causing them to enter entirely into the jar and thereby restraining and stopping them.
Consecrate the water jar twenty-one times with mantras to ward off all obstructive spirits;
place this water jar at the mouth of the mandala in an open space so that its rim touches the ground,
and wait until the wind and rain have ceased and it is calm, pure, and bright.
Thereupon, he removed the jar.
Furthermore, the Venerable Ānanda possessed the mantra of Kāśyapa.

Holding these, perform one thousand and eighty *homa* offerings; this will immediately suppress all the poisonous vapors, calamities, torrential rains, obstacles, and evil winds of all the malevolent nāgas throughout the ten directions, causing them to clear away at once.
It eliminates the calamities of famine for all sentient beings and protects and benefits all crops, flowers, fruits, and seeds,
causing them to ripen fully endowed with excellent flavor.
If it does not clear, double the previous amount of offerings,
performing them once, twice, or even up to five times;
it will certainly clear and cease.
The mantra-holder shall bathe to purify the body and wear clean garments;
severing all speech and discourse,
they shall achieve accomplishment by governing the Dharma with a mind of great compassion according to the Dharma.
Venerable Ānanda, there is furthermore a mantra capable of warding off all evil nāgas and malevolent beasts that devour the sprouts of crops,
and it can also dispel all ghosts and spirits that suck the vital essence from humans.
They all fled and dispersed,
thereby bringing great peace and happiness to all sentient beings in the world.
The crops, fruits, and grains shall always flourish and attain great abundance.
